candidates.title: Guide a workflow template resubmission

demandEvidence.chore: I’m looking for some guidance regarding a workflow template submission that has been rejected three times.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’m looking for some guidance regarding a workflow template submission that has been rejected three times.

ease.reason: An author could test a checklist with supplied example feedback, but the discussion supplies no criteria and no implementation reference supports automation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: workflow authors may pay for submission guidance; this single request proves neither a customer group nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can format author-supplied rules into checks, but useful advice depends on criteria and template details absent from the post.

autonomy.reason: A proposed checklist can flag missing operator-entered items; a person must interpret rejection reasons and decide readiness, with no documented automation support.

evidence.reason: The request directly says a submission was rejected three times and asks for guidance, but gives no reasons or recurring need across authors.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a checklist could organize rules supplied by the author, but the only assigned evidence omits the rejection criteria needed for useful guidance; this same evidence was assessed in recent run loop-40172434668-1.

candidates.title: Draft reminders from spreadsheet due dates

demandEvidence.chore: I want to connect Google Sheets to my Make scenario using the Search Rows module so I can automate reminders based on due dates stored in a spreadsheet.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to connect Google Sheets to my Make scenario using the Search Rows module so I can automate reminders based on due dates stored in a spreadsheet.

ease.reason: A beginner can test operator-supplied due-date rows and draft text, but no supplied implementation reference supports the Sheets connection or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent professional service operators may pay to reduce missed due dates; this discussion proves no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic-data test can identify due rows and draft reminders; live connection, date edge cases and delivery remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed repeated check can flag dates, but a person must verify dates, recipients and drafts; no source documents a working integration.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly names Google Sheets, Search Rows, due dates and reminders, but offers little detail on frequency or operating constraints.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a bounded reminder-draft test is conceivable with synthetic rows, but the integration is not documented and demand detail is limited.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: cybersecurity consultancies may pay for faster rule drafting; this Show HN description establishes neither an unmet buyer need nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week sandbox could draft or revise one rule against synthetic events, but YARA-L correctness and Google SecOps compatibility remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed tool could prepare rule text, but an analyst must validate syntax, test detections and approve deployment; no automation capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The post describes a skill for writing, reviewing, tuning and converting YARA-L rules, but gives no example, measured use or evidence of unmet demand.

candidates.reason: Assessed the exact detection-rule task using a synthetic-event sandbox design. Below threshold: this Show HN post describes an existing skill, not an evidenced unmet service need, and no supplied implementation reference supports safe rule validation or deployment.
